prompt:
A 30-second cinematic episode of an epic space-exploration saga, awe-inspiring and breathtaking, like a nature documentary crossed with a sci-fi epic. This is an ALIEN place — nothing about it should resemble Earth.

The hero: the cyan samurai robot with the horned helmet from the first reference image; its fighter-jet form is shown from several angles in the following reference images — note the sharp pointed nose at the front and the engine exhausts at the rear. The golden glyph cube artifact is the last reference image.

LIGHTING RULE: one distant sun lights everything; consistent light direction and shadows in every shot. No moons.

FLIGHT RULE: whenever the jet flies, it always flies NOSE-FIRST — the sharp pointed nose leads in the direction of travel, engines trailing blue fire. It banks and carves like a real aircraft, never drifting sideways or backwards.

THE WORLD — the Twin Waltz: two planets locked in a fast, close orbit around each other, so close their surfaces fill each other's skies. One is an ember-red canyon world; the other a jade-green ocean world. Between them lies the STILL ZONE — a corridor of zero gravity where their pulls cancel: boulders, glittering dust, ribbons of stolen ocean water and the hulls of ancient abandoned spaceships hang weightless in space, drifting in slow silence while the two planets wheel around them.

PHYSICS RULE: inside the Still Zone everything is weightless — nothing falls; objects drift, tumble slowly, and keep moving when pushed. The robot cannot walk there: it moves by pushing off floating rocks and gliding. On the planets' surfaces gravity is normal.

OPENING (0-3s): deep space. The robot drifts in orbit watching the two planets spin rapidly around each other like dancers, tidal clouds stretching between them — visibly NOT Earth. A small golden holographic counter floats beside its helmet reading exactly "FRAGMENT 003 / 512". The robot dives.

THE DIVE (3-16s): mid-fall the robot transforms into its fighter-jet form and drops nose-first toward the red canyon world. A sweeping continuous flyover: carving through ember-red slot canyons while the jade ocean planet fills half the sky overhead like an impossible ceiling; then pulling up, climbing THROUGH the boundary into the Still Zone — the contrail stops trailing and hangs frozen in space behind it; threading between weightless boulders and the broken hulls of derelict alien spaceships, their dark engines long dead; flying alongside a glittering river of ocean water that arcs through space from one planet toward the other, wobbling in ribbons and spheres. Fast, fluid, majestic — no slow motion.

THE CHALLENGE (16-23s): at the heart of the Still Zone floats the landmark: a slow-turning cluster of boulders and trembling water spheres, and at its center one COLOSSAL water sphere glowing faintly gold from within. The jet transforms back into the robot and glides in — it cannot walk, so it leaps from drifting boulder to drifting boulder, pushing off each one, dodging rocks that collide and tumble around it as the two planets wheel past in the background. One wrong push sends it spinning; it catches the bent antenna boom of a derelict spaceship, corrects, and launches toward the glow.

THE FRAGMENT (23-28s): the robot pierces the surface of the colossal water sphere and swims through its weightless interior to the center, where the artifact from the reference image — a single fist-sized golden metallic cube etched with glowing circuit glyphs — hangs perfectly still. The robot closes both hands around it; the glyphs flare, and for one breathtaking beat every drifting boulder, droplet and wreck in the Still Zone stops and hangs motionless — then slowly resumes its waltz.

THE RITUAL CLOSE (28-30s): close-up on the robot's open palm holding the ONE cube — there is only ever this single cube on screen. Its glyphs pulse and golden holographic text appears in the air beside it reading exactly "FRAGMENT — SECURED" (this exact text, two words only, NO numbers or digits anywhere in it). A calm, epic voice speaks the episode's only words: "Fragment three... secured." Final frame holds on the robot and the single glowing cube, the two planets wheeling slowly behind it.

Audio: the soundtrack is an original epic MOTIVATIONAL anthem with clear English vocals, composed for this episode — soaring and uplifting, drums building through the dive, turning weightless and glassy inside the Still Zone, and peaking as the fragment is taken. The voice sings these lyrics across the episode, timed to the action:

"Let go, let go, there's nothing holding me,
between two turning worlds I'm finally free!
Push off, fly on, the stars are close enough —
even in the stillness, I will never give up!"

The sung anthem is the only sound until the end, where a calm epic voice speaks the single line "Fragment three... secured." No other dialogue, no robotic servo sounds. Vertical 9:16 composition, cinematic lighting, photoreal detail on the landscapes, the robot always crisp and readable. Fast-paced, majestic, unforgettable.
